87703.e: Many millions of years ago there were horsetails as tall as trees, called calamites. They usually grew up to 10 metres tall, some even taller.
87703.m: In the past there were horsetails as big as trees.

87704.q: What partly formed from the ancient forests with giant horsetails?
87704.e: The plants of the ancient swamp forests were pressed together under the ground. Over a very long time they turned into coal.

87705.q: What do the first shoots of the field horsetail look like in spring?
a: Brownish with a cone at the tip
87705.e: In early spring the field horsetail grows brownish shoots. At their tip there is a cone with spores.
87705.m: In spring the field horsetail sends up brown spore shoots.

87706.e: Horsetails have no flowers and no seeds. Like ferns, they are spore plants.

87707.q: How are the small side branches of the horsetail arranged?
a: In a ring round the stem
87707.e: On the horsetail the side branches grow all round in a ring. That is why it looks a bit like a little fir tree.
87707.m: Horsetails look like little fir trees.

87708.q: Which two living things together make up a lichen?
87708.e: A lichen is a partnership. The fungus gives protection and water, and the alga makes food using light.
87708.m: A lichen is a partnership of fungus and alga.

87709.q: What does the alga provide in a lichen?
87709.e: The alga is green and can make sugar using sunlight. The fungus lives on it too. In return the fungus gives protection, a hold and water.
87709.m: In a lichen the alga makes the food.

87710.q: Where do lichens grow, for example?
a: On stones, walls and tree bark
Only under water in the lake
87710.e: Lichens hardly need any soil. They grow on rocks, walls, roofs and tree bark.
87710.m: Lichens even grow on bare stone.

87711.q: Where do you often see the bright yellow sunburst lichen?
a: In the sand by the sea
87711.e: Sunburst lichen forms bright yellow to orange patches. You often see it on walls, roofs and tree bark.
87711.m: Sunburst lichen grows on walls and branches.

87712.q: What does it show when lots of different lichens grow in one place?
87712.e: Many lichens are very sensitive to dirty air. Where many kinds grow, the air is usually clean.
87712.m: Lots of lichens show clean air.

87713.q: Where can lichens live where hardly anything else grows?
a: On rocks high up in the mountains
Inside a stone with no light
87713.e: Lichens can stand cold and dryness well. That is why they even grow on rocks high in the mountains.
87713.m: Lichens survive even on cold mountain peaks.

87714.q: The map lichen looks like a colourful map. What does it grow on?
87714.e: Map lichen grows on stones and rocks, often high in the mountains. Its yellow-green patches with black edges look like countries on a map.

87715.q: Which animal in the far north scrapes away the snow in winter to eat lichens?
87715.e: In winter reindeer scrape away the snow. Underneath they find lichens, an important food.

87716.q: What does a beard lichen look like?
a: Like a grey beard on branches
87716.e: Beard lichens hang from branches in long, grey-green threads. They look like a beard.
87716.m: Beard lichen hangs from branches like a beard.

87717.q: Where do beard lichens hang especially often?
a: On the branches of trees in mountain forests
87717.e: Beard lichens like damp, clean air. In mountain forests they often hang on firs and spruces.
87717.m: Beard lichens often hang in mountain forests.

87718.q: Does beard lichen harm the tree it hangs on?
a: No, it takes no food from it
Yes, it makes it fall over
87718.e: Beard lichen only uses the branch as a place to hold on. It makes its own food and gets water from the air and rain.
87718.m: Beard lichen only uses the tree to hold on to.

87719.q: What does it tell you when lots of beard lichens hang on the trees?
a: The air there is very clean
There are lots of factories there
It has not rained for a long time
87719.e: Beard lichens are especially sensitive to air pollution. Where they grow, the air is clean.
87719.m: Beard lichens only grow in clean air.

87720.q: What colour are beard lichens usually?
87720.e: Beard lichens are usually grey-green or yellowish green. When they are damp, they look greener.

87721.q: Where does beard lichen get its water from?
87721.e: Beard lichens have no roots. They soak up water from rain, dew and fog.
87721.m: Beard lichen drinks rain and fog.

87722.q: What does a beard lichen feel like when it has been dry for a long time?
87722.e: Without water, beard lichen dries out and becomes brittle. After the next rain it goes soft again.

87723.q: What do some birds use beard lichens for?
a: To warm their feet while flying
87723.e: Beard lichens are soft and stringy. Some birds build them into their nests.
87723.m: Some birds build beard lichens into their nests.

87724.q: Where does a fern carry its spores?
87724.e: Ferns have no flowers. Their spores sit in little brown clusters on the underside of the leaves.
87724.m: Ferns carry their spores under their leaves.

87725.q: How big is a single spore?
a: As small as a speck of dust
87725.e: Spores are tiny and light. You can hardly see a single spore without a microscope.
87725.m: Spores are as fine as dust.

87726.e: Spores are so light that the wind carries them far away. This is how they reach new places.
87726.m: The wind carries spores far away.

87727.q: What comes out of a ripe puffball when you press it?
87727.e: The puffball is a fungus. When it is ripe and you press it, millions of brown spores puff out like smoke.
87727.m: A cloud of spores puffs out of a ripe puffball.

87728.q: How many spores can a single fern make?
87728.e: A fern makes huge numbers of tiny spores. Only very few of them land in a good place and start to grow.

87729.q: What does a spore need for something new to grow from it?
87729.e: Spores only germinate if they lie somewhere damp enough. That is why ferns and mosses often grow in damp places.
87729.m: Spores only germinate where it is damp.

87730.q: Where does a mushroom like the button mushroom make its spores?
a: Under the cap on the gills
Deep in the ground on the roots
On top of the cap in flowers
In small fruits on the stem
87730.e: Under the cap of the button mushroom there are thin plates called gills. That is where the spores form.
87730.m: Mushrooms make their spores under the cap.

87731.q: What colour are the ripe spore clusters under a fern frond usually?
87731.e: When the spores are ripe, the clusters are usually brown. Then the spores fall out.
87731.m: Ripe spore clusters are usually brown.

87732.q: What are the large leaves of a fern called?
87732.e: The leaves of ferns are called fronds. They are often finely divided like feathers.

87733.q: What does a young fern frond look like in spring?
a: Rolled up like a snail shell
Straight like a stick with flowers
87733.e: Young fern fronds are rolled up at first. They slowly unroll, like a snail shell opening up.
87733.m: Young fern fronds are rolled up like a snail shell.

87734.q: What is the rolled-up tip of a young fern frond also called?
87734.e: The rolled-up tip looks like the curved staff of a bishop, which is called a crozier. That is why it is also called a crozier.
87734.m: A young fern frond looks like a bishop's crozier.

87735.q: What are the brown dots on the underside of some fern fronds?
87735.e: The brown dots are not a disease. They are spore clusters that the fern uses to reproduce.
87735.m: Brown dots under fern fronds are spore clusters.

87736.q: What shape are most fern fronds?
87736.e: Most fern fronds are divided into lots of small parts. They look like a big green feather.
87736.m: Fern fronds often look like feathers.

87737.q: What do the fronds of a fern grow from?
a: From a rootstock in the ground
87737.e: Ferns have a rootstock in the ground. The fronds grow upwards from it.
87737.m: Fern fronds grow from the rootstock.

87738.q: In which season do most young fern fronds unroll where we live?
87738.e: In spring it gets warmer and brighter. Then the ferns start growing and their fronds unroll.

87739.q: What does the underside of a frond with ripe spores feel like when you run your finger over it?
87739.e: Ripe spores come off easily. That is why brown dust often sticks to your fingers when you touch it.

87740.q: How does the stag's-horn clubmoss grow?
87740.e: The main shoot of the stag's-horn clubmoss creeps across the forest floor. Only short side branches stand upright.
87740.m: Clubmoss creeps along the forest floor.

87741.q: What do the little leaves of clubmoss look like?
87741.e: Clubmoss has lots of small, needle-like little leaves. They sit closely all round the stem.

87742.q: How long can the creeping shoot of the stag's-horn clubmoss get?
87742.e: The main shoot keeps growing across the ground year after year. That way it becomes several metres long.
87742.m: Clubmoss can creep for several metres.

87743.q: Where does the stag's-horn clubmoss make its spores?
87743.e: Yellowish cones sit on upright stalks. Because they look like little clubs, the plant is called clubmoss.
87743.m: Clubmoss carries spore cones shaped like clubs.

87744.q: Who uses clubmoss spores for a bright flash of fire?
87744.e: Fire-breathers blow clubmoss spores into a flame. The fine spores burn at once with a big flash.

87745.q: How big were the relatives of clubmoss many millions of years ago?
a: As small as grains of sand
87745.e: In the time of the coal forests there were relatives of clubmoss as tall as trees, called scale trees. Today clubmosses are only small.
87745.m: In the past there were clubmosses as big as trees.

87746.q: Where does clubmoss grow where we live?
a: In the middle of the lake
87746.e: Clubmosses grow in forests, on heaths and in the mountains. They are rather rare here.
87746.m: Clubmosses grow in forests and on heaths.

87747.q: Does clubmoss stay green in winter?
87747.e: Clubmoss is evergreen. Even in winter you can see its green shoots on the forest floor.
87747.m: Clubmoss stays green all year round.

87838.q: What is kept in a blood bank?
87838.e: Donated blood is stored in a blood bank. From there it goes to hospitals when patients need blood.
87838.m: A blood bank stores donated blood.

87839.q: What is donated blood kept in?
87839.e: Donated blood goes into special, clean plastic bags. They are called blood bags.
87839.m: Donated blood is stored in plastic bags.

87840.q: What is a bag of donated blood called?
87840.e: A bag of donated blood is called a blood bag. It is labelled very carefully.
87840.m: A bag of donor blood is called a blood bag.

87841.q: Where are bags of donated blood stored?
a: In a wooden cupboard in the corridor
87841.e: Donated blood is stored cold. That way it keeps for a few weeks.

87842.q: What must match between the blood of the donor and the person receiving it?
87842.e: Donor blood must match the blood group of the person receiving it. Otherwise it can be dangerous.
87842.m: For a blood transfusion the blood group must match.

87843.q: Which four blood groups are there in the best-known blood group system?
87843.e: In the ABO system there are the blood groups A, B, AB and O. The blood group is written on every blood bag.
87843.m: The four blood groups are A, B, AB and O.

87844.q: Why are new blood donations needed again and again?
a: Blood does not keep for ever
Blood can be made in factories
87844.e: Blood bags only keep for a limited time. That is why the blood bank constantly needs fresh donor blood.
87844.m: Blood banks constantly need new donations.

87845.q: What is it called when a patient in hospital is given blood from a bag?
87845.e: In a blood transfusion, donor blood flows through a tube into a vein. This helps, for example, after a lot of blood has been lost.
87845.m: In a blood transfusion you are given donor blood.

87846.q: Where is blood usually taken for a blood test?
a: From the inside of the elbow
From the top of the ear
87846.e: On the inside of the elbow there are easy-to-see veins just under the skin. Blood can be taken there easily.
87846.m: Blood is usually taken from the inside of the elbow.

87847.q: What is used to take blood from a vein for a blood test?
87847.e: A fine needle is put into the vein. The blood then flows into a small tube.
87847.m: A blood test needs a fine needle.

87848.q: What is often tied around the upper arm before blood is taken?
87848.e: The tourniquet briefly holds back the blood in the veins. Then they stand out more and are easier to find.
87848.m: A tourniquet makes the veins easier to see.

87849.q: Where is a blood sample examined closely?
87849.e: In the laboratory, experts test the blood with machines. That way you find out, for example, whether there is enough iron.
87849.m: Blood samples are examined in the laboratory.

87850.q: Where do you often prick for a single drop of blood?
87850.e: For a little blood, a small prick in the fingertip is enough. This is how blood sugar is measured, for example.
87850.m: For a drop of blood you prick the fingertip.

87851.q: What do you do at the spot where the needle went in after blood has been taken?
a: Press on it and put on a plaster
Have a hot bath straight away
87851.e: If you press on the spot for a moment, it soon stops bleeding. A plaster then protects the tiny wound.
87851.m: After blood has been taken, press on the spot and put on a plaster.

87852.q: What does it mean if you have to come to a blood test “fasting”?
a: Sleep for a long time beforehand
87852.e: Fasting means that you have not eaten anything for a while beforehand. Otherwise some blood values can come out wrong.
87852.m: Fasting means you have eaten nothing beforehand.

87853.q: Which kind of blood vessel is the needle put into when blood is taken from the arm?
87853.e: For blood samples, blood is almost always taken from a vein. In the arm, veins lie under the skin where they are easy to reach.
87853.m: When blood is taken, the needle goes into a vein.

87854.q: From what age can you give blood in Switzerland?
87854.e: In Switzerland you can give blood from the age of 18. Children cannot give blood yet.
87854.m: In Switzerland you can give blood from the age of 18.

87855.q: Roughly how much blood do you give in a blood donation in Switzerland?
87855.e: About 450 millilitres of blood are taken in a donation. That is a little less than half a litre.
87855.m: In a blood donation you give just under half a litre of blood.

87856.q: How much must you weigh at least to be allowed to give blood in Switzerland?
87856.e: Anyone who wants to give blood must weigh at least 50 kilograms. Lighter people have less blood in their bodies.
87856.m: Blood donors weigh at least 50 kilograms.

87857.q: Who does a blood donation help?
a: People who are ill or injured
87857.e: Donated blood is given, for example, to people after an accident or during an operation. It can save lives.
87857.m: A blood donation can save lives.

87858.q: Roughly how long does taking the blood itself last during a donation?
87858.e: The blood flows into the bag in about 10 to 15 minutes. With the questionnaire and resting afterwards, the visit takes a bit longer.
87858.m: Taking the blood during a donation only lasts a few minutes.

87859.q: Can you give blood every week?
a: No, only a few times a year
Yes, as often as you like
87859.e: After a donation the body has to make new blood. That is why you can only give blood a few times a year.
87859.m: You only give blood a few times a year.

87860.q: Why do you have to wait a long time between two blood donations?
a: The body has to make new blood
The blood has to get cold first
The needle has to grow back
87860.e: After a donation the body is missing some blood. It needs a few weeks to replace it.
87860.m: The body needs time between two blood donations.

87861.q: What should you make sure to do after giving blood?
87861.e: After a donation, drinking plenty helps the body replace the lost fluid. You should also rest for a short while.
87861.m: After giving blood you should drink plenty.
